1) Fixed interval: The Bézier curve for the variable \( t \) is defined on the interval [0, 1].
2) End point interpolation: The Bézier curve always starts at the first control point and ends at the last control point, but it does not pass through any other control points.

3) Convex hull: The Bézier curve \( B(t) \) is defined by a collection of control points \( c^i \) that are contained inside the convex hull formed by all these control points. If the control points of the Bézier curve satisfy \( \underline{p} \leq c^i \leq \bar{p} \), \( \forall i \in \{0, 1, \ldots, n\} \), it follows that \( \underline{p} \leq \overline{B(t)} \leq \bar{p} \), \( \forall t \in [0, 1] \)

4) Hodograph: A hodograph is the derivative curve \( B^{(1)}(t) \) of the Bézier curve \( B(t) \) and is always a Bézier curve with control points that follow the equation \( c^{i,1} = n \cdot (c^{i+1,0} - c^{i,0}) \), where \( n \) represents the polynomial degree.
